objective: Run the DPW-8 V1 ONERA OAT15A transonic verification case on the committee-supplied Rizzi grid family, levels 1 through 4, to a converged primal at a single angle of attack, and report a grid-convergence trend on lift, drag and surface pressure against the workshop's own gridding and numerics rulebook
rationale: The scoping report of 2026-07-28 left exactly one open question: nobody had counted the cells in the 2D verification grid bundles, so V1 sat at 'plausible, not confirmed'. That question is now closed by measurement. The Rizzi bundle carries a nine-level structured family and its cell counts were read straight out of the CGNS zone headers rather than trusted from its README: 15872, 34816, 63488, 100352, 144384, 253952, 471040, 667648 and 1146880 cells, all nine matching the README exactly. Levels 1 through 8 are at or below this lab's largest ever converged primal of 579072 cells, and the finest level is only twice it. This is the first Drag Prediction Workshop case found whose committee grids are inside our proven envelope at every offered level, and unlike the Joukowski case already attempted it uses a committee grid rather than one we generated ourselves, on a real transonic condition of Mach 0.73 and chord Reynolds number 3 million

cost_basis: Estimate, bracketed by two measured anchors of our own rather than assumed. Levels 1 through 4 total 214528 cells. Scaling from rung A6 (579072 cells, 38.4 core-min for 1000 iterations) gives about 43 core-min for those four levels at 3000 iterations. Scaling instead from the Joukowski L3 rung (12288 cells, 28.3 core-min for 3000 iterations) gives about 493 core-min, but that rung is known to have been inflated by a linear-solver stall that capped every outer iteration at 1000 sweeps. The estimate of 240 core-min sits between the healthy and the pathological anchor, with headroom for a compressible solver being dearer per cell than the incompressible one A6 used. Memory is not expected to bind: A6 held 30 GB free at 579072 cells, and every level here except the ninth is smaller than that. Dollars: zero, the grids are anonymous public downloads and the 64 MB bundle is already fetched
expected_knowledge_gain: First result this lab would have on a workshop-supplied grid rather than one it generated for itself, which is the difference between checking our solver and checking our meshing at the same time. Also the first honest measurement of how close our pipeline can get to the workshop's mandated convergence bar of about 1e-10, roughly four orders tighter than our production standard, which is the single number that decides whether any future Drag Prediction Workshop entry is credible
launch_prompt: Run DPW-8 verification case V1 on the ONERA Rizzi committee grid family, levels 1 through 4 only, at one angle of attack, converged primal only. The grid bundle is already downloaded to the session scratchpad; re-fetch it from the workshop grid server if absent. Scope, and do not exceed it: a converged primal is the whole deliverable. Do NOT attempt an adjoint or any gradient on this case. Levels 1 to 3 sit below the measured adjoint memory wall of between 63920 and 156089 cells and so a gradient looks tempting; the gradient question is reserved and must be routed through the chief engineer before any adjoint work is started. Convert the CGNS grids rather than regenerating them, since using the committee grid is the entire point. Report the cell count you actually load against the published table and stop if they disagree. Expect the workshop numerics spec (a specifically qualified Spalart-Allmaras variant, adiabatic wall, residuals near 1e-10) to be out of reach on our pipeline; disclose every deviation from it plainly rather than quietly substituting, exactly as the Joukowski report did. Watch for the linear-solver stall that killed the Joukowski fine rung: if the momentum solve caps its sweep count every outer iteration, change the solver for the whole family or for none of it, never mid-family. The geometry is ONERA intellectual property and must be referred to as the ONERA OAT15A with ONERA acknowledged; do not redistribute it. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the workshop concluded in June 2026 and this is an internal verification run.
